audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph David coronation, Jerusalem conquest, and warrior roster, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed against 2 Samuel 5 and 23 for coronation consensus, shepherd-ruler language, Jebusite inhabitants, conquest incentive, Joab's elevation, warrior body counts, food-land defense, Bethlehem water risk, Moabite and Egyptian killings, body-size language, foreign warriors, and Uriah.

verses.restored: All Israel gathered to David at Hebron, saying, Look, we are your bone and flesh.
In past, even when Saul was king, you were one leading Israel out and in; YHWH your Divine said, You shall shepherd my people Israel and be ruler over my people Israel.
All elders of Israel came to king at Hebron; David cut covenant with them there before YHWH, and they anointed David king over Israel according to word of YHWH by Samuel.
David and all Israel went to Jerusalem, that is Jebus, where Jebusites were inhabitants of land.
Inhabitants of Jebus said to David, You shall not come here. Yet David captured stronghold of Zion, which became city of David.
David said, Whoever strikes Jebusites first shall become chief and commander. Joab son of Zeruiah went up first and became chief.
David lived in stronghold; therefore they called it city of David.
He built city around, from Millo and around; Joab repaired/restored rest of city.
David grew greater and greater, for YHWH of armies was with him, in narrator's theology.
These were heads of David's mighty warriors, who strengthened themselves with him in kingdom, with all Israel, to make him king according to word of YHWH concerning Israel.
This is number/list of David's mighty warriors: Jashobeam son of Hachmoni, chief of thirty/three; he lifted spear against three hundred slain at one time.
After him Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of three mighty warriors.
He was with David at Pas-dammim when Philistines gathered for battle, where a parcel of land was full of barley; people fled before Philistines.
They stood in middle of parcel, rescued it, and struck Philistines; YHWH saved by great deliverance, in narrator's interpretation.
Three of thirty chiefs went down to rock to David at cave of Adullam while Philistine camp was in valley of Rephaim.
David was in stronghold, and Philistine garrison was then at Bethlehem.
David longed and said, Who will give me water to drink from well of Bethlehem by gate?
The three broke through Philistine camp, drew water from well of Bethlehem by gate, carried and brought it to David. He would not drink it but poured it out to YHWH.

He said, Far be it from me before my Divine to do this. Shall I drink blood/lives of these men who went at risk of their lives? At risk of lives they brought it. He would not drink. These things the three mighty warriors did.
Abishai brother of Joab was chief of three; he lifted spear against three hundred and killed them and had a name among three.
Among second three he was honored above two and became their commander, but did not attain first three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada, son of a valiant man from Kabzeel, did many acts; he struck two sons/warriors of Ariel of Moab and went down and struck a lion in pit on snowy day.

He struck an Egyptian man of great stature, five cubits; in Egyptian's hand was spear like weaver's beam. He went down with staff, seized spear from Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.
These things Benaiah son of Jehoiada did and had a name among three mighty warriors.
He was honored among thirty but did not attain three; David placed him over bodyguard.
Mighty warriors of armies: Asahel brother of Joab, Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,
Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,
Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite,
Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,
Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah the Netophathite,
Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,
Hurai from wadis of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite,
Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,
sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite,
Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal son of Ur,
Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,

translation_notes: The phrase 'all Israel' expresses the Chronicler's idealized unity and should not erase civil war, Saul loyalists, women, civilians, or dissenting communities.
Jerusalem is an inhabited Jebusite city taken by conquest; renaming it the city of David does not erase prior residents.
David's reward for the first attacker elevates Joab through conquest and incentivizes lethal competition.
Warrior body counts are heroic rhetoric, not models of masculinity or sanctity.
The barley-field defense concerns food and livelihood, but Philistine deaths remain human deaths.
David's casual longing prompts subordinates to risk their lives. Pouring out the water recognizes the cost but does not erase leader responsibility for requests made under unequal power.
Moabite and Egyptian opponents may not be racialized, animalized, or treated as spiritually inferior.
Great stature and unusual bodies are not monstrosity, disability, or proof of threat.
The roster includes Ammonite, Hittite, Moabite, and other foreign-associated warriors, undermining ethnic-purity myths.
Uriah the Hittite's name at verse 41 must recall David's abuse of Bathsheba and command murder; warrior honor cannot bury royal guilt.
safety_note: Do not turn David's coronation into leader cult, Jerusalem's capture into modern conquest entitlement, body counts into masculinity, or foreign opponents into racial enemies. Keep Jebusite residents, risked subordinates, killed opponents, and Uriah's betrayal visible.
